Huawei Canada has an immediate permanent opening for a Researcher. 
 About the team: 
 The Huawei Human-Machine Interaction Lab unites global researchers, engineers, and designers to redefine human technology relationships through user centered, hands on research. We focus on agentic AI and multimodal interaction (voice, touch, vision, gesture) across smartphones, wearables, and emerging devices—advancing agentic workflows, multi-agent orchestration, and intuitive human-AI interfaces. By tightly integrating sensing, algorithms, and systems, our prototype driven work ships directly to products, enabling seamless task delegation and human AI collaboration at scale. 
 About the job: 
 Contribute to research and exploration at the intersection of intelligent devices, AI experiences, and emerging interaction paradigms, with a focus on how human-computer interaction is evolving in the AI era and how established and emerging interaction approaches may work together. 
 Bring together technological capabilities, user needs, device form factors, and real-world scenarios to identify high-value interaction problems and opportunities. 
 Propose novel interaction concepts, mechanisms, and system-level approaches that address concrete challenges people face with intelligent systems, leveraging possibilities enabled by evolving technology. 
 Turn interaction concepts into concrete scenarios, use cases, and testable proposals, and collaborate with design, engineering, and technology teams to validate key assumptions and experiential value through prototypes and experiments. 
 Evaluate interaction solutions with appropriate user research and technical methods, covering efficiency, learnability, understandability, controllability, trust, and quality of collaboration, and continuously iterate solutions based on findings. 
 Stay current with emerging interaction paradigms, AI capabilities, and intelligent hardware trends, and translate valuable technologies, products, and research developments into concrete interaction explorations and product opportunities. 
 Collaborate with AI, software, hardware, sensing, design, and product teams to advance promising interaction concepts toward implementable system solutions, technical proposals, patents, or product directions. 
 The total target annual compensation for this position ranges from $106,000 - $156,000 depending on education, experience, and demonstrated expertise. 
 About the ideal candidate: 
 Master's or PhD in Human-Computer Interaction, Interaction Design, Industrial Design, Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, Human Factors, Cognitive Science, or a related field. We welcome candidates from diverse disciplinary backgrounds. 
 Genuine curiosity about emerging technologies, with a habit of actively experimenting with new products, tools, and technologies to discover the interaction opportunities they could unlock. 
 Hands-on experience in interaction innovation, intelligent systems, consumer electronics, digital products, or interaction research, design, or engineering. 
 Strong interest in, and solid understanding of, how evolving AI capabilities may shape human-computer interaction, including how new intelligent interactions can work alongside traditional GUIs, input devices, and established user behaviors. 
 Ability to generate valuable ideas for open-ended interaction problems and develop them into clear concepts that can be discussed, iterated on, and tested. 
 Strong systems thinking, with an understanding of relevant technical capabilities and constraints and the ability to work with design and engineering teams to move solutions forward. 
 Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to explain interaction ideas clearly across research, design, engineering, and product teams. 
 Familiarity with one or more relevant methods, such as user research, experimentation, or system evaluation, and the judgment to choose the right approach for each problem. 
 Experience advancing interaction ideas into prototypes, system concepts, technical solutions, patents, or product directions is an asset.

Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human
 Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.
This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.
 About the OIN Team
 The Okta Integration Network (OIN) is the platform that lets Okta customers discover, connect, and manage third-party applications and identity providers — from single sign-on and provisioning to newer, higher-order integration patterns as the ecosystem of connected software (including AI agents) continues to grow. It's core infrastructure: the workflows OIN powers run continuously for a very large share of Okta's customer base.
 Our team builds and operates all of OIN — from the foundational data model, APIs, and security posture every integration in the network is built on, to the tools partners and customers use to build, test, and ship integrations, to the systems that power what those integrations can actually do once connected. In practice that spans connector metadata and provisioning primitives, partner-facing tooling, and the infrastructure work that keeps a very large, long-lived system fast, secure, and easy to extend as the network grows.
 We're actively expanding OIN's scope beyond its original SSO-and-provisioning core — including new integration patterns as AI agents and machine-to-machine access become part of the identity landscape, and a lower-friction path for partners to bring new integrations into the network. You'd be joining at a point where the platform's scope is visibly widening, working closely with product, architecture, and design to help figure out what "right" looks like as much as building it.
 About the Role
 As a Staff Software Engineer on the OIN team, you'll be a technical leader for a platform a very large share of Okta's customers depend on every day. You'll independently own complex, ambiguous problems end-to-end — from technical scoping through design, delivery, and production operation — partnering closely with product, architecture, and design to help figure out what "right" looks like as much as building it. You'll also be expected to raise the technical bar for the engineers around you, not just deliver your own code.
 We're looking for self-motivated engineers who think from first principles, take pride in high-quality software, and are genuinely kind and collaborative to work with.
 What you'll be doing
 Lead discovery and technical scoping for new requirements, turning ambiguous product asks into a concrete architecture, phased delivery plans, and credible estimates, in close partnership with product, architecture, and design.
 Design and evolve the APIs, data models, and security posture that OIN's integrations depend on, with an eye toward backward compatibility and long-term extensibility.
 Drive technical decisions across ambiguous, multi-team dependencies, aligning stakeholders across engineering, product, and other parts of the business when the "right answer" isn't obvious yet.
 Modernize and evolve a large, long-lived production system incrementally without disrupting the customers and integrations that depend on it every day.
 Maintain a high bar for security, testing, and code quality, including vulnerability remediation and threat-aware design, while keeping a real sense of urgency on customer-impacting work.
 Own the production health of the systems you build by writing root-cause analyses when things break, driving follow-through on the fixes, and building the observability that prevents repeat incidents.
 Champion AI-native engineering practices by using AI coding assistants and AI-augmented workflows as a core part of how you design, build, review, and ship software, and helping the team adopt them well.
 Mentor and raise the technical bar for the engineers around you, and represent the team's technical point of view in cross-functional forums.
 What you'll bring to the role
 8+ years of professional software development experience, with a demonstrated history of technical leadership and mentorship.
 Deep proficiency in Java (our primary backend language) or a comparable strongly-typed backend language/framework, with the judgment to know when and how to modernize a large, long-lived codebase without disrupting the customers depending on it.
 Proven experience designing, building, and operating complex, large-scale distributed systems in a cloud environment (AWS, GCP, or Azure), including caching, asynchronous processing, and data migrations at scale.
 Real depth in identity and access protocols (OAuth 2.0/OIDC, SAML, and/or SCIM) and the security instincts that come from having built systems that other companies' software authenticates against.
 Experience designing and evolving APIs and integration frameworks that external developers or partners build on, not just internal consumers. You think about backward compatibility, versioning, and developer experience as first-class concerns.
 Comfortable driving technical direction across ambiguous, multi-team dependencies. You can align product, architecture, and other engineering teams around a plan when the "right answer" isn't obvious yet.
 A security- and compliance-aware mindset — comfortable working on systems where correctness failures have real customer or compliance consequences, not just availability ones.
 Applies AI tools thoughtfully across the development lifecycle, from code generation to review to testing, and can help a team adopt them well, not just use them personally.
 Excellent written communication — you bring structure to ambiguous problems and drive them to closure using first principles, in writing that others can act on without you in the room.
 Extra credit
 Experience integrating with large, specialized third-party enterprise systems that carry their own strict compliance or data-handling requirements.
 Experience running or contributing to a self-serve developer platform or partner/ISV ecosystem.
 Front-end proficiency (React or similar) is a big positive.
 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent experience.

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


 

Role overview:

North is Cohere’s AI workspace platform for enterprises: a secure, customizable environment where companies can use AI across their real workflows while maintaining control over sensitive data. North connects AI agents with workplace tools, applications, and business context, helping users delegate complex work, build automations, inspect outputs, and collaborate with AI in production environments.



As North becomes more capable, one of the most important questions is also one of the hardest: how do we know whether the model is actually getting better for the workflows customers care about?



This role is about being the voice of North inside modelling. You will build the evaluation systems, feedback loops, and applied modelling workflows that make sure model progress translates into better product outcomes for North users. You will work closely with North product teams, customer-facing teams, and modelling teams to define what “good” means across the product surface, turn real usage and product direction into high-quality evals, and use those evals to guide model selection, patches, and regular model updates.



This is neither a pure research role nor a conventional product engineering role. It is a rigorous applied MLE role for someone who cares deeply about measurement, model behavior, and real-world product quality. You should be excited by the craft of building careful evals: evals that capture messy agentic workflows, reflect actual customer needs, resist superficial benchmark hacking, and provide useful signal for where the product and models need to go next.


Please note: this team works closely across Europe and East Coast North America time zones. We are open to candidates who can collaborate effectively within those hours.



Key responsibilities:

 - Own the eval strategy for North: define what we need to measure across agent workflows, tool use, enterprise knowledge work such as deep research, document creation or editing, and other human-AI interactions.

 - Build high-quality evals from the realities of the product: user feedback, production failures, privacy-preserving usage logs, internal dogfooding, customer needs, and forward-looking product goals.

 - Create systems that continuously turn what North is learning from users, customers, and feature teams into evals, so measurement keeps pace with the product rather than becoming a static benchmark.

 - Be the voice of North inside modelling: extract clear insight from eval results, customer-derived data and product context, then turn model failures, capability gaps, and North-specific needs into actionable recommendations for the central modelling teams.
   

Qualifications:

 - You have improved LLM-powered, agent-powered, or AI-product systems through evals, feedback loops, data curation, prompting, model adaptation, or model selection.

 - You care deeply about evaluation as a craft: representative tasks, precise rubrics, clean data, failure analysis, regression tracking, and knowing when a metric is giving false confidence.

 - You have strong applied MLE judgment and can reason clearly about model behavior, eval validity, product outcomes, and production tradeoffs.

 - You are comfortable working close to users and product teams, while translating messy qualitative signals into measurement that other modelling teams can act on.

 - You are self-directed, practical, and motivated by open-ended problems where the right answer requires both technical depth and product understanding.

 - You care about making AI systems genuinely useful in real enterprise settings, not just better on abstract benchmarks.

ValPay builds embedded payments for software companies. Our PayFac-as-a-Service model lets ISVs offer payments to their merchants under their own brand, while we handle underwriting, compliance, and risk. Our partners serve healthcare, legal, hospitality, professional services, and other vertical markets.
 Launching a payments product is the easy part. The value is created when ISV partners go live, their merchants enroll, and transactions flow. We’re hiring a product marketing Lead whose success is measured by adoption: how quickly and how deeply partners and merchants use our products.
 You’ll own positioning, launches, and lifecycle marketing across our vertical markets and across North America, Europe, and APAC. You’ll report to the CEO and work closely with product, sales, partnerships, the ISV channel team, and operations. 
 AI should be part of how you work. Use it to research, draft, analyze, and automate. You’re responsible for the quality of the result.
 What we value 
 Sound judgment and attention to detail.
 Measuring success by what customers do, not by what we shipped.
 Taking responsibility and finishing work without being chased.
 Understanding how the business makes money and caring about results.
 The honesty to say when something isn’t working, including your own work.
 What you’ll do 
 Drive partner and merchant adoption: You’ll own the adoption journey end to end: signature, integration, go-live, first transaction, merchant enrollment, and expansion. The hardest gap is between “integrated” and “actively transacting,” and you’ll be the person who finds out where partners and merchants stall and designs programs to close it. That means lifecycle campaigns, onboarding content, and activation playbooks for two audiences at once: the ISV partner and the merchants who use their software. With the ISV channel team, you’ll run co-marketing and merchant-enrollment campaigns that lift penetration within each partner’s customer base.
 Measure adoption and act on it: You’ll build and maintain the adoption dashboard: activation rate, time to first transaction, attach and penetration rate, volume per merchant, feature adoption, and cohort retention. You’ll use that data to segment partners and merchants, flag at-risk accounts, and surface expansion opportunities, then take what you find to the teams who can act on it.
 Own positioning and messaging: You’ll develop the positioning, value propositions, and messaging for each product and vertical, and for new verticals and markets as we enter them. A central part of this is explaining clearly how our embedded payments offering differs from horizontal PayFacs, processors, and ISOs. You’ll translate technical capabilities into the outcomes ISVs and merchants care about: revenue share, retention, cleaner reconciliation, and faster onboarding.
 Run launches built around activation: You’ll lead launch plans for new products, features, verticals, and regions. Every launch gets adoption targets and a 30/60/90-day activation plan, not only awareness goals. You’ll also make sure what we’re building is communicated publicly, online and through partners. You’ll adapt messaging to regional regulatory and market conditions, and work with product, finance, risk, and support so that each launch is commercially and operationally ready before it goes out.
 Equip sales, partnerships, and support: You’ll create the sales playbooks, pitch decks, battlecards, case studies, ROI calculators, and objection-handling guides that sales and partnership teams use, and equip support to explain the products as well. You’ll train teams to sell for activation, not just signature. You’ll run win/loss and churn analysis and feed what you learn back into positioning and the product.
 Represent the market inside the company: You’ll track competitors, pricing, interchange, and regulatory developments, and be the voice of the market and of adoption data in product planning. When acquisitions or product consolidations happen, you’ll support portfolio and integration messaging.
 What you’ll bring 
 At least 3 years of experience in product marketing at a B2B software, fintech, or payments company.
 A track record of running launches and measuring them on adoption or usage, not only on awareness.
 Experience marketing to two audiences at once, such as partners and their customers, or platforms and their users.
 Working knowledge of how card payments work, or the ability to learn it quickly and explain it accurately.
 Comfort with data. You can define a metric, build or spec a dashboard, and draw a conclusion from it.
 Strong writing. You can turn a technical capability into a clear business case for a software company or a small-business owner.
 Experience building sales enablement that teams actually used.
 You can take a loosely defined goal, set your own plan, and finish it.
 You use AI tools every day for research, drafting, and analysis, and you check what they produce.
 Useful experience 
 Embedded payments, PayFac, or ISV channel experience.
 Lifecycle or onboarding marketing in a partner-led business.
 Marketing in healthcare, legal, hospitality, or professional services software.
 Launching products in Europe or APAC.
 Running win/loss or churn analysis programs.
 Hands-on experience with SQL, a BI tool, or marketing automation.
 Portfolio or integration messaging after an acquisition.
 Who will enjoy this role 
 You notice when a partner has been live for two months and only a handful of their merchants have enrolled, and you want to know why. Is it the pitch, the onboarding, the partner’s own sales team, or the product?
 In the same week you might rebuild a merchant onboarding email sequence, pull cohort data for the CEO, train a partnership team on a new vertical, and rewrite a battlecard after a lost deal to a horizontal processor.
 The scope is wide for one person, and adoption is a harder target than launch coverage. You’ll be judged on numbers you influence but don’t fully control, which means working through partners, product, and sales to move them. Priorities will shift with the roadmap and with acquisitions.
 Why this role matters 
 ValPay is building products and features for software partners across several verticals and regions. That work has limited impact unless partners and merchants know about it, understand it, and use it.
 You’ll work directly with the CEO to decide how our products are positioned and how each launch turns into transactions. Your work affects how quickly partners go live, how many of their merchants enroll, and how much volume flows through the platform. You’ll have the authority to set the story and change it when the adoption data says so.
 _______________________________________________________________________________________
 ValPay conçoit des solutions de paiement intégrées pour les entreprises de logiciels. Notre modèle PayFac-as-a-Service permet aux éditeurs de logiciels (ISV) d’offrir des paiements à leurs commerçants sous leur propre marque, pendant que nous prenons en charge la souscription, la conformité et la gestion des risques. Nos partenaires servent les secteurs de la santé, du droit, de l’hôtellerie et de la restauration, des services professionnels et d’autres marchés verticaux.
 Lancer un produit de paiement, c’est la partie facile. La valeur se crée lorsque les ISV partenaires sont mis en service, que leurs commerçants adhèrent et que les transactions circulent. Nous recherchons une personne responsable du marketing produit dont le succès se mesure à l’adoption : la rapidité et la profondeur avec lesquelles les partenaires et les commerçants utilisent nos produits.
 Vous serez responsable du positionnement, des lancements et du marketing du cycle de vie dans l’ensemble de nos marchés verticaux, en Amérique du Nord, en Europe et en Asie-Pacifique. Vous relèverez du chef de la direction et travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes produit, ventes, partenariats, canal ISV et opérations.
 L’IA devrait faire partie de votre façon de travailler. Utilisez-la pour faire de la recherche, rédiger, analyser et automatiser. Vous êtes responsable de la qualité du résultat.
 Ce qui compte pour nous 
 Un bon jugement et le souci du détail.
 Mesurer le succès à ce que font les clients, et non à ce que nous avons livré.
 Prendre ses responsabilités et mener le travail à terme sans qu’on ait à faire de relances.
 Comprendre comment l’entreprise génère des revenus et se soucier des résultats.
 L’honnêteté de dire quand quelque chose ne fonctionne pas, y compris dans son propre travail.
 Ce que vous ferez 
 Stimuler l’adoption par les partenaires et les commerçants : Vous serez responsable de tout le parcours d’adoption : signature, intégration technique, mise en service, première transaction, adhésion des commerçants et expansion. L’écart le plus difficile à combler se situe entre « intégré » et « en transaction active », et c’est vous qui déterminerez où les partenaires et les commerçants stagnent et qui concevrez des programmes pour combler cet écart. Cela comprend des campagnes de cycle de vie, du contenu d’accueil et d’intégration (onboarding) et des guides d’activation pour deux publics à la fois : l’ISV partenaire et les commerçants qui utilisent son logiciel. Avec l’équipe du canal ISV, vous mènerez des campagnes de comarketing et d’adhésion des commerçants qui augmentent le taux de pénétration au sein de la clientèle de chaque partenaire.
 Mesurer l’adoption et agir en conséquence : Vous créerez et tiendrez à jour le tableau de bord de l’adoption : taux d’activation, délai avant la première transaction, taux de rattachement et de pénétration, volume par commerçant, adoption des fonctionnalités et rétention par cohorte. Vous utiliserez ces données pour segmenter les partenaires et les commerçants, repérer les comptes à risque et faire ressortir les occasions d’expansion, puis vous transmettrez vos constats aux équipes qui peuvent agir.
 Définir le positionnement et les messages : Vous élaborerez le positionnement, les propositions de valeur et les messages pour chaque produit et chaque marché vertical, ainsi que pour les nouveaux marchés à mesure que nous y entrons. Un volet central de ce travail consiste à expliquer clairement en quoi notre offre de paiements intégrés se distingue des PayFac horizontaux, des processeurs de paiement et des ISO. Vous traduirez les capacités techniques en résultats qui comptent pour les ISV et les commerçants : partage des revenus, fidélisation, rapprochement simplifié et intégration plus rapide.
 Mener des lancements axés sur l’activation : Vous dirigerez les plans de lancement des nouveaux produits, fonctionnalités, marchés verticaux et régions. Chaque lancement comporte des cibles d’adoption et un plan d’activation sur 30, 60 et 90 jours, et pas seulement des objectifs de notoriété. Vous veillerez aussi à ce que ce que nous construisons soit communiqué publiquement, en ligne et par l’intermédiaire des partenaires. Vous adapterez les messages aux conditions réglementaires et commerciales de chaque région, et travaillerez avec les équipes produit, finances, risques et soutien pour que chaque lancement soit prêt sur les plans commercial et opérationnel avant sa sortie.
 Outiller les équipes des ventes, des partenariats et du soutien : Vous créerez les guides de vente, présentations, fiches concurrentielles, études de cas, calculateurs de RCI et guides de réponse aux objections qu’utilisent les équipes des ventes et des partenariats, et vous outillerez également l’équipe du soutien pour qu’elle puisse expliquer les produits. Vous formerez les équipes à vendre en visant l’activation, et pas seulement la signature. Vous mènerez des analyses des gains et des pertes ainsi que de l’attrition, et réinjecterez vos apprentissages dans le positionnement et le produit.
 Représenter le marché au sein de l’entreprise : Vous suivrez les concurrents, les prix, les frais d’interchange et l’évolution de la réglementation, et serez la voix du marché et des données d’adoption dans la planification des produits. Lors d’acquisitions ou de regroupements de produits, vous soutiendrez les messages liés au portefeuille et à l’intégration.
 Ce que vous apporterez 
 Au moins trois ans d’expérience en marketing produit dans une entreprise de logiciels B2B, de technologie financière ou de paiements.
 Une expérience concrète de lancements dont le succès a été mesuré par l’adoption ou l’utilisation, et pas seulement par la notoriété.
 De l’expérience à faire du marketing auprès de deux publics à la fois, par exemple des partenaires et leurs clients, ou des plateformes et leurs utilisateurs.
 Une connaissance pratique du fonctionnement des paiements par carte, ou la capacité de l’acquérir rapidement et de l’expliquer avec justesse.
 De l’aisance avec les données. Vous savez définir un indicateur, concevoir ou spécifier un tableau de bord et en tirer une conclusion.
 D’excellentes aptitudes en rédaction. Vous savez transformer une capacité technique en argumentaire d’affaires clair pour une entreprise de logiciels ou le propriétaire d’une petite entreprise.
 De l’expérience dans la création d’outils d’habilitation des ventes que les équipes ont réellement utilisés.
 Vous savez prendre un objectif vaguement défini, établir votre propre plan et le mener à terme.
 Vous utilisez des outils d’IA tous les jours pour la recherche, la rédaction et l’analyse, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.
 Atouts 
 Expérience en paiements intégrés, avec des PayFac ou dans un canal ISV.
 Marketing du cycle de vie ou de l’accueil et de l’intégration des clients dans une entreprise axée sur les partenaires.
 Marketing de logiciels dans les secteurs de la santé, du droit, de l’hôtellerie et de la restauration ou des services professionnels.
 Lancement de produits en Europe ou en Asie-Pacifique.
 Mise en place de programmes d’analyse des gains et des pertes ou de l’attrition.
 Expérience pratique de SQL, d’un outil de veille d’affaires (BI) ou d’automatisation du marketing.
 Messages liés au portefeuille ou à l’intégration à la suite d’une acquisition.
 Ce poste vous plaira si… 
 Vous remarquez qu’un partenaire est en service depuis deux mois et que seule une poignée de ses commerçants ont adhéré, et vous voulez comprendre pourquoi. Est-ce l’argumentaire, l’accueil et l’intégration, l’équipe de vente du partenaire ou le produit?
 Au cours d’une même semaine, vous pourriez refaire une séquence de courriels d’accueil pour les commerçants, extraire des données de cohortes pour le chef de la direction, former une équipe de partenariats sur un nouveau marché vertical et réécrire une fiche concurrentielle après avoir perdu un contrat au profit d’un processeur horizontal.
 La portée du poste est vaste pour une seule personne, et l’adoption est une cible plus difficile à atteindre que la visibilité d’un lancement. Les priorités évolueront au gré de la feuille de route et des acquisitions.
 Pourquoi ce poste est important

 Vous travaillerez directement avec le chef de la direction pour décider du positionnement de nos produits et de la façon dont chaque lancement se traduit en transactions. Vous aurez l’autorité nécessaire pour définir le discours et le modifier lorsque les données d’adoption l’indiquent.

Hi 👋🏾 I’m Abhik https://www.linkedin.com/in/abhikpramanik, Ashby's Co-Founder and VP of Engineering. We’re looking for a versatile, persistent product engineer who’s not afraid to set up reusable building blocks across the stack and advocate for the time and space to do so. At Ashby, all our engineers ship features end-to-end at a high pace. Example is the best leadership. We’ll give you the room to do your best work, and you'll be our guide! If that speaks to you, read on.

What Ashby gives you in return is the best of both early and growth-stage environments. The agency and no-nonsense of a seed startup: you write product specs, make product and design decisions, and build in an almost-no-meeting culture. While also the product-market fit and scale of a growth-stage startup: 100,000+ weekly active users who depend on your software and eagerly await your next feature.

We have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet.

You’ve probably seen this role posted before, and it’s because we’re always expanding the team (we’re on track to double Engineering this year). We’re bubbling with ideas for how to support Talent Acquisition with software, and we recently launched Talent Management products https://www.ashbyhq.com/add-ons/people-workflows to expand our total addressable market and become a company worth $60B+.

We read every application and aim to respond to yours within 3-4 days (often sooner).

 


ABOUT THE ROLE AND HOW WE WORK

Our engineering culture strives to recreate the environments where we did our best work as ICs – where we had the ownership and agency to impact our users with creative and innovative software.

I started my career building software for artists in the Visual Effects industry. It was a formative experience for me as a software engineer because success relied on my ability to be a product manager and designer. I talked to artists to understand their needs. I came up with ideas. I did industry research, designed interfaces, and prototyped ideas. I watched artists use what I built and decided what to tackle in the next iteration. No daily stand-ups, no t-shirt sizing, no planning meetings.

I studied computer science to solve problems, not tickets, and this felt exactly like that. I not only felt creative and fulfilled but the agency and ownership we were given as engineers powered an incredible amount of innovation.

Innovation came differently (or not at all) at technology startups beyond the seed stage, often through an engineer’s force of will and ability to push back against culture (rather than any encouragement from it). Engineering was narrowed to implementation and delivery, partly due to the influence of other departments and partly due to the influx of "Agile" processes like sprint planning. In those companies, I felt like a JIRA jockey. 

At Ashby, we’re building an environment that is optimistic about what engineers can own and achieve. An environment that embraces innovative engineers, and, frankly, often stays out of their way. As a Product Engineer, you’ll take ownership over a large portion of one of our products and own projects end-to-end (wearing hats traditionally worn by product and design). You’ll research competitors, write product specs, make wireframes, and more. To ground it with examples, product engineers at Ashby have:

 - Designed and built automated interview scheduling. This feature automates scheduling by calculating possible times from a pool of interviewers and other constraints, and then presenting these times to the candidate for selection via our responsive web app. This solves the “Calendar Tetris” problem I talk about in "What We're Building."

 - Built a generalized declarative filter architecture that allows users to create complex filters for any record with a consistent UI and compile it to SQL in our backend. Many user-facing features use it.

 - Specced, designed, and implemented a feature that allows users to complete signing offers entirely within Ashby. This project involved talking to customers to understand their requirements, deciding what technologies to use, building a prototype, and working with other team members to integrate the final implementation into additional features.

 


WHAT WE’RE BUILDING

As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition (TA) software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.

Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 🥵 TA software didn’t help.

As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!

As we’ve set the standard for excellence in TA software, HR teams have pulled us into solving their problems in areas like onboarding and performance management.

 


WHY YOU SHOULD OR SHOULDN’T APPLY

Software engineers come in many flavors, not all of which fit our model. Here are some things  to help you decide if this fits you and what you’re looking for:

 - You’re not afraid to tackle any part of a technology stack. You do what’s necessary to successfully deliver a feature, whether writing frontend or choosing new infrastructure. We’ll provide a supportive environment to do it successfully (e.g., design system, SRE team).

 - You’ve tackled projects with a lot of product and technical ambiguity, and you thrive at the intersection of the two. We’re not building a simple CRUD app, and many of the challenges we tackle require you to use your knowledge of our customers to build powerful abstractions and flexibility in the system to solve a class of problems.

 - You know how to strike the right balance between speed and quality. Ashby wasn’t built quickly. We took four years to launch publicly because convincing customers to switch required a high-quality product. However, time isn’t infinite, especially for a startup, so we still move with urgency—we’ve built the equivalent of three or more VC-backed startups with a very small team.

 - You are ambitious and always looking to improve your skills. For most engineers, this role will give you more freedom and responsibilities than you’ve experienced in the past. To thrive (and level up), you’ll need to be open to feedback (and we give lots of it).

 - You’re an excellent collaborator and communicator. Ownership and freedom don’t mean you work in a vacuum. You’ll need to vet your decisions with the appropriate stakeholders, keep them up to date when necessary, and work with other engineers to get your projects across the finish line. Clear and concise communication helps a lot here!

 - You seek to create leverage in your work. The nature of software is that you can often automate or abstract what would be tedious, time-consuming work. Your impatience usually leads to new abstractions, tools to allow Support to debug before Engineering, new lint rules to prevent common bugs, etc. 

Put another way, you shouldn’t apply if:

 - To you, a tech lead, staff, or principal engineer is someone who spends most of their time project managing or doing architecture reviews. Our most tenured engineers spend most of their time building, and we often trust them with our most challenging problems. While they lead product and technical areas and help other engineers plan their most challenging work, it’s not a requirement, nor do engineers need their sign-off.

 - You need company-driven process and structure to get your projects across the finish line. Sprint planning and well-defined project management processes are things you need or look to others to lead. You’d rather focus on the technical details and challenges.

 - You only want to do exciting work. We’re building a team of kind, collaborative folks. Customer issues and investigations are distributed across the team, including our high-level ICs.

 - You can get lost in the details. Once you start implementation, it can be hard to take a step back and think about the project as a whole. You like everything to be planned upfront.

 - You haven’t led or taken ownership of projects before. You’re used to working with tech leads and taking on tasks distributed by them.

 - You want to mentor earlier-career engineers. We rely on engineers owning their projects, so we need engineers with that experience. This requires the team to be reasonably tenured. More than 90% of the team would be considered Senior or above in the industry today, so mentorship opportunities are very limited.

 


ENGINEERING CULTURE

Our engineering culture is motivated by Benji’s (my Co-founder and CEO) and my belief that a small, talented team, given the right environment, can build high-quality software fast (and work regular hours!). We do it through:

 - Minimal process with ownership over decisions normally made by product and design

 - Natural collaboration and deliberate communication

 - Investing in tools and abstractions that give us leverage

 - Putting effort into building a diverse team

 


MINIMAL PROCESS & LOTS OF OWNERSHIP

The best engineers we’ve worked with delivered reliably magical outcomes. They took customer problems and relentlessly drove them to solutions that were not only successful but often brilliant and creative. While they did this with minimal oversight, stakeholders were never in the dark as to what was going on, and no setback was a surprise.

Traditional product-development processes aren’t meant for the best engineers. Their purpose is to create consistent outcomes regardless of the engineer’s skill. But, consistency comes at the expense of an engineer’s time and freedom—both ingredients necessary to generate those magical outcomes. As a result, process stifles the best engineers and doesn’t give others the opportunity to practice the behaviors that made the best engineers the “best.”

At Ashby, we want to build an environment that encourages every engineer to be their best. So, at Ashby, every Engineer runs their project. Product Managers (and Designers) build strategy, do customer research, and hand off problem briefs to Engineers. Engineers take on the rest: they research the problem, write product specs, build wireframes, and implement their solution end-to-end. We rely on engineers, not process, to push information outward to the relevant folks (e.g., Product Managers) and pull folks in to help (e.g., Designers, Infra). It’s a new level of ownership for many engineers, but we’d rather an engineer fail a bit and coach up their skills than use process as a crutch. Not everyone succeeds in our culture, but those who do thrive.

 


COLLABORATION IS NATURAL & COMMUNICATION IS DELIBERATE

Our engineering team consists of lifelong learners who are talented but also humble and kind (meet them here https://www.ashbyhq.com/team!). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally. We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers are in <2h meetings per week (I wrote about it here https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/company/thoughtful-communication).

To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over 4 years. ~34 hours of focus time, 2.5h of interviews, and 3.5 hours of meetings:

 
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/4ea5f68e-c33e-4ac9-831a-e732bee4a303/d4679311-9dba-4031-bf5e-19ce78597ab1/calendar.png]
 

We also meet in person at least twice a year, once as a department and once as a company. You also have a small budget to meet up with folks in your city/region.

 


INCREASE LEVERAGE, NOT TEAM SIZE

We built Ashby with the quality, breadth, and depth that many customers would expect from much larger teams over larger time scales. We’ve done this through investment in:

 - Great developer tooling. Our CI/CD takes ~10m, and we deploy at least 15x a day. A debugger that works out of the box. Everyone on the team has contributed to our developer experience 💪🏾.

 - Building blocks to create powerful and customizable products fast. At the core of Ashby is a set of common components (analytics modeling and query language, policy engine, workflow engine, design system) that we constantly improve. Each improvement to a common component cascades throughout our app (short video below).

 - AI-powered tooling. We think of AI as a way to automate the mundane parts of building and maintaining high-quality software. We use a combination of third-party and internally built tools that, for instance, auto-triage customer issues, suggest fixes, prototype ideas, generate production-ready code, and conduct code reviews. Engineers have an unlimited token budget (but are not measured on it). We write in detail about our philosophy, current use of AI, and future plans for AI in Engineering here https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/engineering/ai-ashby-engineering-and-the-future.

Here’s an impromptu quote from Arjun in our company Slack of what it’s like to build a feature at Ashby:

 
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/4ea5f68e-c33e-4ac9-831a-e732bee4a303/8d94727a-46d8-42a2-9627-ddcd7f822f95/arjun.png]
 

And a demo of one of these building blocks:




PUT EFFORT INTO DIVERSITY

Diverse teams drive innovation and better outcomes. Having seen my mother and partner build their careers as minority women in non-diverse fields, I want to make sure Ashby creates opportunities for the next generation of engineers from underrepresented groups.

Today, 25% of engineers and 50% of our engineering leaders at Ashby are from underrepresented groups. We are taking conscious steps to improve, like sourcing diverse candidates, providing generous paid family leave, no leetcode interviews, and more.

 


WORK-LIFE BALANCE: IT’S A MARATHON, NOT A SPRINT

The intensity of work at Ashby should feel like a marathon, not a sprint (nor speed-walking). We work with urgency and ambition to build excellent software, but we don’t need to prove out a new software category or product-market fit. That requires ingenuity and thoughtfulness, and that doesn’t happen with unrealistic deadlines or sleepless nights.

Our remote, low-meeting, high-ownership culture gives you a lot of flexibility in how you structure your days and weeks. In practice, that means you keep your own hours, but there will be moments of intensity, like launching your feature at our annual user conference. We offer unlimited PTO, and you actually get to use it. Some of our most exceptional engineers take almost 30 days of vacation per year.

This way of working allows many of us on the team to be active parents, including Benji and me. I block off 1.5 hours every morning to spend with my daughter and drop her off at school.  Mujda https://www.linkedin.com/in/mujdaalamzai/ (Product Engineer) puts it best in an article https://nextplayso.substack.com/p/should-you-join-ashby about us: “I can say that Ashby is a great place to be a mom… No one bats an eye if I have to take my kid to a doctor’s appointment or have to work weird hours because childcare fell through.”

 


INTERVIEW PROCESS

At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. We’ll dive into past projects and simulate working together via pair programming, writing product and tech specs collaboratively, and talking through decisions. There are no leetcode or whiteboard exercises.

Our interview process is three rounds:

 1. Introduction call with Hiring Manager (15 to 30m, live)

 2. A technical screen where we pair in our actual codebase (1h, live)

 3. Three non-coding interviews that focus on product thinking, technical design, and infrastructure (3h 15m, live can be split across multiple days)

Depending on our leadership team’s bandwidth, we may start with an additional 30m screen with a recruiter.

Your hiring manager will be your main point of contact and prep you for interviews. Each round will have written guidance so you know what to expect (you’ll need minimal preparation). You’ll meet 4 to 6 people in engineering (with 5-15 minutes in each interview to ask them questions). If we don’t give an offer, we’ll provide feedback!

 


YOUR FIRST THREE MONTHS AT ASHBY

We want an exceptional onboarding experience for every new hire. At Ashby, your dev environment is set up with a single script, you push your first product change on day one, and you spend the rest of your time shipping product changes that give you a tour of our codebase and best practices. The product changes increase in scope and ambiguity from simple copy changes to the delivery of a prominent, impactful feature. Your manager will do a 30, 60, and 90-day review to give feedback and calibrate on how we work together.

It’s a team effort to get you successfully onboarded; you’ll have a peer paired with you to answer questions, pair program, and check in often to see if you need help. The rest of the team will run training sessions on our culture, product, engineering process, and technical architecture.

 


TECHNOLOGY STACK

I’m sharing our tech stack with the caveat that we don’t require previous experience in it (but a love of typed languages is helpful 😀): TypeScript (frontend & backend), React, GraphQL API, Node.js, Postgres, Redis.

When they joined Ashby, many of our engineers switched from other languages like Swift and Kotlin (Ben https://linkedin.com/in/benasher44/), platforms like iOS (Tom https://www.linkedin.com/in/tom-quist-0925a199/) and Windows (Adam https://www.linkedin.com/in/adam-lusch/). We care more about fundamentals (e.g., debugging, abstractions) and how fast you learn. For folks on the team who switched, it's nice seeing changes hot reload versus waiting for XCode to compile 😅.

 


BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary and equity.

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - Unlimited PTO, and we will encourage you to take it.

 - A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. For folks outside the US, it may be longer to be in line with regional requirements.

 - Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

 - $250/month tool budget plus access to Claude, Cursor, and Codex with generous token budgets.

 - If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, also fully covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

Hi, I’m Loren https://www.linkedin.com/in/lfoseid/, the Head of Strategic Customer Success here at Ashby. My team is dedicated to building deep, consultative partnerships within the Enterprise space. 

Our Customer Success Team is passionate about shaping and scaling an exceptional upmarket customer experience across the Enterprise Segment. We’re thrilled to be hiring our next Strategic CSM as we continue to grow the team.

Role Requirements:

 - You have a strong track record of customer success experience in B2B SaaS (at least five years), supporting the implementation and adoption of complex technologies through the customer journey.

 - You’re comfortable managing a book of ~20 strategic customers, exceeding $2m in total ARR. You enjoy multi-threading, developing relationships across a broad set of stakeholders while supporting existing teams to drive adoption and retention.

 - You have experience working closely with cross-functional stakeholders across Sales, Marketing, Product, and Operations.

 - You love becoming a product and industry expert. You create ‘Ah ha!’ moments by tailoring configuration, driving product adoption, and crafting training to address a customer’s specific challenges so they achieve their intended business outcomes.

 - You’ve worked with technically complex products and show a strong curiosity to explore details and understand how things work.

You Should Apply If:

 - 📣 You communicate with precision and clarity. You can take something complex (like a multi-layered report or a nuanced workflow) and explain it simply and confidently.

 - 🎧 You are a listener first. You seek to understand what customers actually need and then advocate for them internally to shape how Ashby evolves for enterprise use cases.

 - ⚙️You thrive in complexity. Ashby is powerful and highly configurable; you’re energized by learning a product with depth, and you can translate that knowledge into creative solutions for your customers.

 - 🧑‍🏫 You’re excited to help shape a new segment. Our Strategic customer motion is still evolving; you’ll be iterating on playbooks, helping us learn what works, and turning those learnings into repeatable processes for the team.

 - 🔍 Your peers describe you as detail oriented. You send crisp follow-up emails, on time. You take pride in internal operations, like real-time CRM updates.

 - 📊 You are always looking for ways to improve your work through data.

 - 👥You may have been a recruiter, hiring manager, or interviewer before. That experience helps you quickly connect Ashby’s workflows to real-world hiring problems (though it’s not required).

Why you shouldn’t apply:

 - You prefer managing a broad, high-volume book of business (if so, see our Mid-Market or Startup roles).

 - You're interested in managing customer accounts with infrequent and well-defined touchpoints (rather than excited by the fluidity required of early stage CS work).

For renewal negotiation and upsell, we have a remarkable team of Contract Managers. As such, this role does not currently include variable pay, aligning with our strategy to hire product-oriented CSMs rather than adhering to the conventional Account Manager model.

Performance Marketing Lead — Total Life
 Full-time · Remote (North America) · Reports to the CEO 
 The short version
 We spend real money to reach older adults who need mental health care, and most of them are not on the internet the way your last audience was. We need someone who can grow ROAS on channels that already work, and who has the range to build demand in places a growth marketer usually never touches — direct mail, radio, print, community events, CTV.
 If you have only ever optimized inside Meta Ads Manager, this is not your role. If you have personally owned budgets across paid digital and offline, and can show what happened to CAC when you did, keep reading.
 About Total Life
 Total Life is a national behavioral health telehealth platform built for later-life adults. 200+ licensed clinicians, 49+ states, and we bill Original Medicare Part B directly — which means for most of the people we serve, therapy costs them little to nothing. That's an unusually strong offer, and our job is to get it in front of the people who need it.
 We ranked #5 in the healthcare category on the Inc. 5000, with growth over 5,000% since 2021. We are still small enough that this hire will change the trajectory of the company.
 What you'll own
 Full-funnel paid acquisition across Google, Meta, YouTube, Bing, Reddit, Quora, Nextdoor, and native networks — plus whatever you can prove out next.
 Traditional and offline demand generation. Direct mail, print, radio, CTV/linear, community and senior-center partnerships. Our audience is 65+, and a large share of our best prospects will never click an ad. You'll be responsible for building programs that reach them anyway, with attribution good enough to defend the spend.
 ROAS and CAC as your scoreboard. Not impressions, not MQLs. You own blended CAC, channel-level ROAS, and cost per completed intake.
 Creative strategy. You'll direct the concepting, testing, and iteration of ad creative — you don't have to be the designer, but you have to know what to test and why, and you have to be able to tell a creative team something more useful than "make it pop."
 Measurement infrastructure. Attribution across a long, offline-heavy funnel is genuinely hard here. You'll define how we know what's working, including for channels with no click.
 Budget allocation. You'll bring us a monthly plan for where the money goes, defend it with numbers, and change it when the numbers change.
 What we're looking for
 Non-negotiable: 
 You have personally managed $30K+/month in spend on multiple individual channels — not a $30K/month total book split six ways. We want to see depth, at scale, on more than one channel.
 Direct experience on both digital and traditional/offline channels. Real spend, real results, in both worlds.
 A track record you can put numbers to: starting ROAS, ending ROAS, over what period, on what spend, and what you actually changed to get there.
 Fluency in the analytics stack — GA4, ad platform reporting, a CRM (we run HubSpot), and enough comfort in spreadsheets or SQL to check your platforms' math rather than take their word for it.
 You test aggressively and kill your own ideas quickly when the data says to.
 Strong pluses: 
 Healthcare, Medicare, insurance, or another regulated-advertising category.
 Marketing to seniors, or to adult children making decisions for a parent.
 Direct response with a phone-based or human-assisted conversion path.
 You've built a channel from zero, not just optimized an inherited one.
 How to apply
 Skip the cover letter. Send us:
 One channel you scaled. The channel, the monthly spend, the ROAS or CAC before and after, the time frame, and the two or three specific decisions that moved it. Numbers or it didn't happen.
 One channel you shut down. What you spent, what you learned, and how fast you called it.
 Your first-90-days hypothesis for us. Look at our ads, our site, and our offer. Where would you put the next $50K, and what would you expect to get for it? Two paragraphs is plenty — we're reading for thinking, not polish.
 Equity options
 Health, dental, vision 
 Generous PTO
 Remote-first with a home office or equipment stipend.
 A learning/conference budget

 Behavox is a cloud-native AI company providing an integrated controls platform for global banks, asset managers, hedge funds, private equity firms, insurance businesses, and commodity firms.  Behavox is a high-performance organisation with a strong bias toward delivery, ownership, and responsibility. We commit, and we execute. We are building systems that are complex, mission-critical, and global in scale; systems that many consider too large or too difficult. To do that, we seek the smartest, most technically capable engineers and technologists who take end-to-end responsibility and want to win by building what others cannot.

 About the Role 
 The Senior FP&A Analyst owns Behavox's core financial model — its architecture, the accounting beneath it, and the forecasts and analysis the company plans and decides by. The role exists to change decisions, not report them: it turns the numbers into the choices leadership actually faces. It reads and integrates budgets into the model, but does not run the budgeting cycle.
 The same analyst builds the valuations, scenarios, and pro-forma models behind every acquisition — evaluating targets, running diligence, and folding closed deals into a single consolidated view. This work is periodic and must be carried alone when it arrives; the steady state is the operating model and SaaS forecasting.
 This is a high-autonomy role that works without a detailed brief and sets the modeling standard others build on. It is accountable for the accuracy and integrity of the numbers, and for turning them into recommendations sharp enough to act on — the downside case included, not just the point estimate — for senior leadership, the board, and investors. It pressure-tests the assumptions behind every result, works fluently with modern tooling and AI, and compounds that edge by learning relentlessly. Its influence comes from the rigor and reach of the analysis, not from authority: it owns the model and the truth it tells, not the decisions made from it.
 What You'll Bring 
 Financial Model & Accounting Foundations — Understands the architecture of integrated three-statement and operating models and the accounting that underpins them, including SaaS revenue recognition and cost treatment. Understands how the company's budgets are built and how to integrate them accurately into the core financial model.
 Forecasting & SaaS Unit Economics — Understands bottom-up short-term forecasting, driver-based long-term modeling, and the SaaS metrics that reveal business performance. Connects movements in those metrics to their underlying drivers and the operating levers that can change them.
 Mergers, Acquisitions & Integration — Understands acquisition valuation, purchase accounting, combined-entity projections, and consolidation mechanics sufficiently to evaluate targets and integrate completed acquisitions into the financial model.
 Business & Commercial Acumen — Understands in depth how the business and its functions generate revenue and incur costs, including the underlying revenue drivers, cost structure, and operating levers. Applies this knowledge to identify inconsistencies and challenge financial results and assumptions.
 Financial Systems & AI Tooling — Understands Google Sheets, Excel, AI, and automation capabilities sufficiently to determine how they should be applied to financial modeling and analysis. Distinguishes where automation can improve speed and control from where financial judgment and manual validation must remain.
 What You'll Do 
 Financial Model Ownership — Builds and maintains the core three-statement and operating model using robust architecture, accounting logic, scenario and sensitivity layers, and integrated budgets, owning the accuracy of every output and the integrity of every assumption to provide reliable forecasts and analysis for company planning and decision-making.
 Acquisition Modeling & Integration — Builds valuations, scenarios, and pro-forma combined-entity models by independently evaluating targets, supporting due diligence, and consolidating closed deals to provide a complete financial view of acquisition implications and the combined business.
 Business-Review Reporting — Drives the financial substance of monthly, quarterly, and annual business reviews with the broader FP&A team by translating model outputs and performance drivers into a clear narrative that enables senior management, the board, and investors to understand results and their implications.
 Metrics Analysis & Business Partnering — Diagnoses financial and SaaS metric movements by identifying operating drivers, pressure-testing assumptions, and modeling relevant levers and downside cases to give decision-makers evidence-based recommendations they can act on.
 AI-Enabled Productivity — Applies AI and spreadsheet automation to recurring financial workflows by automating appropriate work and strengthening data validation while retaining judgment over what remains manual to reduce cycle time without compromising financial integrity.

Providius is looking for an experienced Senior Software Engineer, Test to help us build stronger, faster, and more reliable ways of validating complex software systems.
 This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who enjoys writing code, building automation, debugging difficult problems, and improving how software gets tested across an engineering organization.
 Position Overview 
 This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role. You will spend most of your week writing test code, building test infrastructure, and working directly with engineers, not writing test plans for others to execute.
 We are looking for someone to take our test automation and quality engineering practices to the next level. You will build the automated test suites and tooling underneath them, raise the standard for how the engineering team tests its own work, and help ensure our quality practices keep pace with how quickly modern software is now developed.
 Software gets written and changed faster than it did even a few years ago. AI-assisted development accelerates that further, but it also changes where defects come from and what traditional reviews and test suites may miss. We want someone who sees that as an engineering problem: building the coverage, tooling, feedback loops, and development practices that allow the team to move quickly without sacrificing reliability.
 Our products also increasingly include AI and machine-learning functionality, including LLM-based assistants and integrations with AI clients. These systems introduce a different class of testing problem. Outputs may vary between runs, model or prompt changes can alter behaviour without traditional code changes, and quality may need to be measured across a set of results rather than with a simple pass or fail.
 You do not need to be an ML researcher, but you should have experience testing software with AI, ML, LLM, or other non-deterministic components and understand how to build credible evidence that these systems are ready to ship.
 You will have meaningful autonomy and responsibility. You will work with engineering leadership to identify our biggest quality risks, establish practical approaches to addressing them, and implement the automation and tooling needed to make those approaches part of everyday development.
 Duties and Responsibilities 
 Design, write, and maintain automated test suites across unit, integration, API, end-to-end, and regression testing
 Build and improve test infrastructure including fixtures, mocks, reusable test libraries, test data management, and simulation environments
 Build and maintain CI/CD test gates, smoke tests, regression suites, coverage reporting, and automated release-readiness checks
 Keep automated testing fast, reliable, and useful enough that developers trust it and use it regularly
 Build API and contract testing across services and integration boundaries
 Establish performance, load, stress, and soak testing for high-throughput and real-time systems
 Investigate and debug difficult failures across application, service, database, infrastructure, and deployment boundaries
 Work with engineers to determine appropriate test coverage and validation approaches for new features and systems
 Review test code with the same engineering standards applied to production code
 Help developers improve the quality and testability of their own code rather than making testing the responsibility of a separate QA silo
 Build reusable patterns and tooling that make it easier for engineers to write good tests
 Establish practical testing standards and help drive their adoption across engineering
 Identify gaps in existing test coverage and determine where deeper or different forms of validation are required
 Help adapt our testing practices to the increased pace and changing failure modes introduced by AI-assisted software development
 Use modern development and AI tooling to improve the speed and effectiveness of test development while maintaining confidence in the results
 Validate that automated tests actually detect incorrect behaviour rather than simply confirming the current implementation
 Share testing practices, tooling, and lessons across the engineering team
 AI and ML Quality 
 Build and maintain evaluation approaches for AI, ML, and LLM-based product features
 Test non-deterministic systems using representative datasets, repeated evaluation, appropriate metrics, and acceptance thresholds
 Establish regression testing for model, prompt, retrieval, and AI-system changes
 Test AI integrations end to end, including tool use, schemas, authentication, authorization, error handling, and unexpected responses
 Help determine where automated evaluation is sufficient and where human review remains necessary
 Validate data and pipelines used to support AI and ML functionality
 Incorporate production failures and edge cases back into automated test and evaluation suites
 Help define evidence-based release criteria for AI-enabled product functionality
 Tech Stack 
 Our engineering environment includes: 
 Languages: Python, Java, TypeScript
 Test frameworks: pytest, JUnit, Playwright or Cypress
 API and performance testing: Postman, k6 or JMeter
 Data: PostgreSQL, TimescaleDB
 Infrastructure: Linux, Docker
 CI/CD: automated pipelines, test gates, coverage and release validation
 Development tools: JIRA, Bitbucket
 AI and ML systems: Python-based ML and LLM tooling, model and data pipelines, LLM integrations, and Model Context Protocol (MCP)
